note: The walking skeleton. Two acceptance criteria are Deferred and neither is a gap: AC1.5.1 and AC1.5.3 are the profile EDITING screen, which U3 enables by creating Profile with its RLS policy but which is exercised at B5, where the enrollment flow provides a second actor to test the boundary against. Everything the privacy boundary itself needs - the table split, the policy, and the non-superuser test role - lands here. BR4.4, deferred to this Unit by U2, is discharged by BR2.7. Added while drafting: BR6.3, because B3's confidence hypothesis needs an Owner row and an Enrollment row that no U3 code may create. A committed seed script supplies them as a verification precondition; an INSERT inside U3 would be the ownership transfer BR6.1 forbids, arriving disguised as a fixture.

coverage.target: BR2.2, BR5.1, BR5.3 - issue path; a real SMS through the adapter, success being response_code 202 and nothing else
BR2.3, BR4.2 - verify within 5 minutes returns a token pair; the teacher lens is then resolved per request by BR1.1 rather than carried in the token
BR2.3 - expires_at compared server-side; a client-supplied timestamp would make the window advisory
BR2.3 - the 6th attempt is refused AND the code is dead afterwards, so a correct 7th also fails. An implementation that counts without invalidating passes only the confirmatory half
BR5.3 - every non-SENT outcome surfaces as a delivery failure with a resend after cooldown, never as an incorrect code. A timeout is UNKNOWN because the SMS may have been delivered
BR6.2 and the Android surface in functional-spec §3 - the number is typed, never read from the SIM, and no SMS read permission is held

BR1.1 - a dormant record created by a teacher is claimed on first successful verify, without an invitation. Account.activated_at is the column that distinguishes dormant from signed-in; the lenses that then appear are computed by BR1.1 from the enrollments already recorded against the number
BR1.1 - both lenses are offered because both queries return rows. No stored role decides it
BR1.1 - holds for free rather than by a check: a number appearing only as a student is offered only a student lens because the guardian query returns nothing
BR1.1, BR1.4 and functional-spec §3 - the switcher sends a hint and decides nothing; the server re-derives the lens, so no re-authentication is needed
U3 creates Profile and its RLS policy; the profile EDITING screen belongs to the Android surface and is exercised at B5, where the enrollment flow gives it a second actor to test against
BR3.1, BR3.2 - two name columns, two writers, two tables. Which name a teacher sees is answered by which table the query reads
Helper text on the profile screen; same reason as AC1.5.1
BR2.2 - per-number 3/hour and 5/day, checked before the gateway call
BR2.2 - per-IP-prefix 10/hour
BR2.1 - datastore-backed counters. The test must FAIL against a per-process dictionary, which is the obvious implementation and stops working with two workers
BR2.5 - the global daily ceiling refuses and alerts
BR2.6 - degraded mode says temporarily unavailable, never invalid number, and never reveals the limit
BR2.4 - otp_hash never otp; the test reads the column and asserts it differs from what was sent
BR2.7 - byte-identical responses AND the same hashing work on both paths. This is NFR14.4, deferred here by U2's BR4.4, asserted structurally and never as a wall-clock bound
BR1.1 - computed from Owner and Enrollment at that moment; no role column on Account, which is an absence that cannot be misread
BR1.2 - a named rule rather than an incidental test, because its only purpose is to fail against the caching implementation
BR1.3 - the mirror of BR1.2 and the more dangerous direction, since it GRANTS access the data no longer supports
BR1.4 - the memo lives on the request object, so it is garbage-collected with the request. The location is the control
BR4.1, BR4.2, BR4.3 - rotation with family invalidation, hashed storage, enforced expiry, JWT kid with two valid keys
BR2.1 through BR2.7 - all seven abuse controls, each with an adversarial rather than confirmatory test
BR4.1, BR4.2, BR4.3 - 15-minute access token, 30-day rotating refresh with reuse detection and family invalidation
BR3.1, BR3.2, BR3.3 - the table split and row-level security. U2 shipped the third layer; BR3.3 is what makes the suite non-vacuous
BR6.2 and functional-spec §3 - no device identifier is transmitted and the number is never read from the SIM
BR2.7 - the structural-equivalence obligation U2 deferred to this Unit is discharged here, with its limitation recorded rather than overstated
U4 - the enrollment flow warns before creating. This Unit supplies the fact the warning rests on, since BR1.1 can tell whether a number owns a batch, but the flow itself is U4's
U4 - and the second lens then appears for free under BR1.1, with no re-authentication and no stored role, which is the point
U11 - deletion moved out of this Unit deliberately, so the paths are specified once against the full schema rather than twice
U11 - same reason. Requires every table's disposition, which only exists once the schema is complete
U11 - idempotent re-deletion
BR5.5 and functional-spec §3 - the OTP code the app produces renders in Latin numerals. The rendering specification settled at OQ-B1-1 fixes Western digits throughout
U4 - server-side collation applies to lists of people, and this Unit renders no such list
BR5.5 and functional-spec §3 - OTP entry is one of the five named screens, and both language bundles ship on screen one so a Bangla layout break is found here rather than on screen forty
U4 - no free-text a person typed is stored by this Unit; the self-entered profile name is written through the profile screen at B5
U4 and U8 - numeric input fields. The OTP field accepts digits but the code is generated server-side, so no normalisation boundary exists here
U8 - transaction IDs belong to the payment path
U2 owns the schema-level assertion; this Unit's refusals carry the single non-disclosing code U2 registered
U4 - a guardian requesting a non-child enrollment needs the enrollment flow to exist
U7 - a student requesting a fee cycle needs fee cycles
BR2.7 - the refusal carries retryable:false and discloses nothing about existence, which this Unit demonstrates on the OTP issue path where both branches are byte-identical
U4 - teacher-lens response schemas need a roster to return. BR3.1's table split is what makes it hold when they arrive
BR1.1 and functional-spec §2.4 - an unsupported lens hint is refused rather than silently resolved to a different lens

BR1.1, BR6.2 - three of the five PUBLIC_ROUTES open here and the refresh route goes in LENS_EXEMPT_AUTHENTICATED, which is why U2 kept that set separate. Every other route this Unit adds resolves a lens through BR1.1, and U2's harness checks that against the real app object
BR1.1, BR1.4 - one account holding two lenses switches without re-authenticating, and no data resolved under one lens is served under the other because each request re-resolves

reverse.target: No AC covers the transport scheme; it comes from contract-summary §C.4.2 and RC-1/RC-2/RC-3. Plain HTTP serves the same API with no redirect and no HSTS - verified against the live endpoint - so a misconfigured http:// ships the phone number AND the OTP in cleartext and succeeds silently

No AC covers adapter selection; it comes from OQ-3a. BulkSMSBD has no sandbox, so team.md's non-production rule cannot hold as written and is satisfied by a null adapter that is the DEFAULT, so a missing setting fails toward not sending

AC9.3.1 - and a cost constraint with no AC behind it: one Bangla character would force UCS-2 and halve the segment budget. The SMS Retriever app hash consumes 12 characters of the 160, which is easy to forget until the invoice arrives

No AC covers the shell tables; it comes from unit-of-work.md and a Units Generation learning. Empty is not absent: lens resolution queries all three tables, and a query against a table that does not exist fails - this nearly shipped a skeleton that could not pass its own verification command

No AC behind it; it comes from B3's own confidence hypothesis, which requires an account that OWNS ONE BATCH and is enrolled as a guardian - neither of which U3 may create. The empty-shell rule answered the SCHEMA question and left the DATA question open, and they are not the same. Without a seed script the skeleton can prove the OTP path and the ABSENCE of a lens and nothing else, so the single most structurally unusual decision in the system goes undemonstrated at the one checkpoint built to demonstrate it
